interpretation: Company mode. Tallyhive's supplied homepage defines the offer: central recipe, ingredient and allergen data with label printing, from GBP 350 per site per month. Geography is the UK. Priorities below are research recommendations, not confirmed customer segments. Supplied pages are treated as captured sources; their claims are attributed where independent verification is unavailable.
summary: Prioritise UK food manufacturers with multi-site technical responsibility, followed by bakery groups and central kitchens supplying multiple outlets. Lead with the Technical Manager: the supplied vacancy explicitly assigns allergen management, label approval, BRCGS readiness and technical budget ownership [S2]. Competitor case studies support manual data handling and central-control/local-printing needs, but no accessible independent buyer reviews were obtained [S5][S6]. Recommend targeted technical-team outreach and educational distribution through the Food & Drink Federation's food-safety and labelling ecosystem [S8]. segments.description: UK catering operations managing recipe information centrally while accommodating local products, prices and label formats. A competitor describes a historical rollout to more than 200 UK catering sites; this is not a current market-size estimate.
segments.priority_reason: Recommended third priority: competitor evidence supports substantial data-handling and integration needs. Qualify integration complexity before pursuing large accounts; Tallyhive's integration capabilities are not evidenced.

Recommendation: control product information centrally while enabling daily label printing at outlets [S6].
Recommendation: reduce manual transfer and matching of ingredient data into label fields [S5].
Recommendation: support technical-team label approval and audit preparation; validate required evidence exports before promising them [S2].
Recommendation: preserve risk-assessment-based PAL decisions rather than treating a label generator as a substitute for allergen controls [S7].

Two undated Planglow customer case studies were read as vendor-selected context, not counted as review/forum voices. No buyer-pain quotes are reported.

triggers.evidence: The supplied 2026-10-20 Technical Manager vacancy combines two-site allergen ownership, label approval, BRCGS readiness and budget management. Inference: a new remit creates a useful discovery moment, not proof of purchase intent.

objections: Inference: GBP 350 per site per month needs a site-level business case; willingness to pay, implementation fees and contract terms are unverified [S1].

Inference: technical teams will ask how data changes, approvals and local permissions are controlled. These are evidenced workflow concerns, not verified Tallyhive features [S2][S5][S6].
Inference: software cannot itself establish that a 'may contain' statement is justified; official guidance requires risk assessment and risk-management actions [S7].

The supplied PAL notice's 2026-07-01 publication and 2027-01-01 expected application date were not independently corroborated. Preserve this as a reported planning signal, not a verified statutory deadline.

Tallyhive's price, positioning and customer relationships are homepage claims. No product demonstration, contract terms, integrations, approval workflow or compliance guarantee was independently verified.

report_markdown:
## Summary
Prioritise UK food manufacturers with cross-site technical responsibility, then bakery groups and central kitchens. Tallyhive states that it centralises recipe, ingredient and allergen data and prints labels, starting at GBP 350 per site per month. These are vendor claims, not independently tested capabilities. [S1]

The strongest initial contact is the Technical Manager. The supplied vacancy explicitly combines problem ownership with technical-budget responsibility; executive sign-off remains unknown. [S2]

## Segments
| Priority | Segment | Why it fits |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Multi-site food manufacturers | Two-site allergen, label and audit responsibilities sit with a budget-owning technical role. [S2] |
| 2 | Bakery groups | Central information, local printing and frequent product changes appear in a competitor case study; an own-site source confirms geographic and operating fit. [S6][S9] |
| 3 | Central kitchens and caterers | Competitor evidence shows central data management, site variations and integration needs. [S5] |

These priorities are recommendations. No defensible market counts or employee-size bands were established.

## Buyer and user roles
**Technical Manager:** evidenced budget holder and inferred champion. **Operations Director:** inferred executive sponsor because the technical role reports there. **General Manager:** potential bakery champion, evidenced discussing the workflow. **Recipe/menu systems product manager:** potential integration champion. **Site chefs and printing staff:** operational users. Only technical-budget ownership is explicit; do not assume final purchasing authority. [S2][S5][S6]

## Jobs to be done
Recommended discovery focus: maintain consistent ingredient and allergen information; approve labels; reduce manual data transfer; coordinate central information with outlet printing; and support audit preparation. These jobs follow the offer, vacancy and competitor evidence, rather than a representative buyer survey. [S1][S2][S5][S6]

## Pains in their words
No accessible independent buyer posts or reviews were obtained, so no pain quotes or voice counts are reported. Capterra blocked the fetch. [S4] Two vendor-selected case studies discuss manual data handling, rapid changes and obsolete packaging stock; they inform hypotheses but are not independent pain validation. [S5][S6]

## Buying triggers
Recommended signals include a new cross-site technical appointment, audit preparation, new products, ingredient changes and expansion of distributed printing. Except for the dated vacancy and historical rollout, purchase intent is inferred. [S2][S5][S6]

The supplied notice reports updated PAL guidance published on 2026-07-01 with expected application from 2027-01-01. Retain that as a reported planning signal. The official PAL page inspected supports risk-assessment-based decisions but does not corroborate this timetable; do not present it as a verified legal deadline. Its stated scope is England, Wales and Northern Ireland, not all UK jurisdictions. [S3][S7]

## Objections
Likely objections are per-site cost, migration effort, compatibility with specification/menu systems, and confidence in data controls. These are inferences to test. A competitor's bespoke integration indicates potential complexity, not a Tallyhive capability. Software must not be positioned as replacing cross-contact assessment. [S1][S2][S5][S7]

## Where they gather
| Verified place | Recommended use |
|---|---|
| Food & Drink Federation food-safety and labelling hub | Test educational content and relevant partnership opportunities; audience size and acquisition performance are unknown. [S8] |

## Tools they trust
LabelLogic Live adoption is documented in vendor-selected case studies, not independent trust research. The vacancy requires specification-system experience, while the catering case describes an unnamed menu-management system. These are incumbent workflows to discover, not assumed replacement targets. [S2][S5][S6]

## Example companies
| Company | Evidence and qualification |
|---|---|
| Harrowgate Foods | Supplied own-site vacancy supports two-site fit; Tallyhive reports it as a customer. [S1][S2] |
| Jenkins Bakery | Own site confirms South Wales branches; competitor case study supports labelling-workflow fit. Not a confirmed Tallyhive prospect. [S6][S9] |

## Messaging implications
Recommendations: demonstrate an ingredient change through to printing; lead with the stated shared-data offer; quantify the buyer's own administration and label-stock costs. These angles rest on vendor material and role evidence, not independently validated buyer language. Avoid absolute compliance promises and unverified deadline claims. [S1][S2][S5][S6][S7]

## Gaps
Independent buyer language, market sizing, broader competitor customers, purchasing authority, integration capability and channel economics remain unverified. Research stopped at the prescribed search/fetch limits; partial pages and blocked reviews were not treated as substantive evidence. [S4][S10][S11]
